$comment: Where the simulation rig is. One file, because seven scripts each carried
their own copy of the address as a parameter default, and a default aimed
at a decommissioned machine is worse than no default: it points somewhere
The Windows administrator password is deliberately not stored here.
Pass -Password or set DELUNO_LAB_PASSWORD for scripts that need WinRM.
The rig's Deluno sign-in password is not stored here either: scripts read it from DELUNO_LAB_APP_PASSWORD, so deluno.password stays null.
$serviceAccount: Who the rig's services run as. null means SYSTEM, which is right when
everything the services touch is local.
A library on a network share is the reason to change it: a SYSTEM process
authenticates to SMB as the machine account, not as a user, so a workgroup
NAS refuses it. That, not networking, is why the old VM could never reach
$mediaBoundary: The owner's real library shares a NAS with the test run, and the NAS
account Deluno uses can write to the whole share. Nothing on the NAS
refuses a write, so assert-media-boundary.ps1 refuses instead: every path
Deluno could write to must sit below isolatedRoot, and nothing may sit
below a protected root or on a drive letter mapped to the share.
